incidents.name: MinimalForwarder spoofed keeper on Base
incidents.notes: KiloEx's MinimalForwarder.execute() let any caller supply both the forwarded `from` address and a signature that its verification accepted, so the attacker impersonated the privileged price keeper and called setPrices() on the KiloEx price feed, opening and closing a position across a self-set price.

sources.ref: callTracer review of the Base attack tx: the attacker contract 0xd649a087... calls 0x3274b668... with selector 0x47153f82 (MinimalForwarder.execute), which delegatecalls impl 0xbed75e25a63d2be11605038921aa5eef78bb4e61 and then calls the price feed 0xfdc7bc3a... with 0xac9fd279 (setPrices); the forwarder proxy was created by KiloEx deployer 0x1d568fc08a1d3978985bc3e896a22abd1222abcf, not by the attacker (public writeups often point at the attacker-deployed 0xd649a087... instead)

incidents.name: MinimalForwarder spoofed keeper on BSC
incidents.notes: Same MinimalForwarder.execute() signature-binding flaw on the BSC deployment: the attacker relayed a forged keeper call to setPrices() and traded against the price it had just written.

sources.ref: callTracer review of the BSC attack tx: attacker contract 0xcc6a5784... calls 0xad37c86c... with 0x47153f82 (MinimalForwarder.execute, impl 0xd8240094e57bf5f893420ffc1e750c94de4a4177) between openPosition/closePosition calls on the KiloEx router 0x298e94d5494e7c461a05903dcf41910e0125d019; forwarder creator is KiloEx deployer 0x1d568fc08a1d3978985bc3e896a22abd1222abcf
